newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: DE BEERS DROPS AFTER HALF YEAR RESULTS.
newsitem.headline: DE BEERS DROPS AFTER HALF YEAR RESULTS.

text.p: Shares in diamond gaint De Beers Ltd dropped on Wednesday as the market digested the firm's interim results published on Tuesday.
"They were a little disappointing and have come off," one dealer said. De Beers stock was down 600 cents to 157.00 rand by 0805 GMT.

De Beers raised its attributable earnings for the six months ended June 1997 to $507 million from $482 million a year ago. Analysts polled by Reuters had forecast net attributable earnings of between $510 and $543 million.
Outgoing chairman Julian Ogilvie Thompson said the firm could see little improvement at the full-year in its balance sheet if Angolan diamond production was affected.

Most of Angola's production is in UNITA-held areas which continue to be a bone of contention between the former rebel movement and the Luanda government since the signing of a peace treaty ending nearly two decades of civil war in 1994.
Thompson said the finalisation of a contract for Russia's diamonds to be sold through its London-based Central Selling Organisation (CSO) was also another niggling worry.

"That (improvement in the next half) depends very much... on the Angolan situation, how much comes out of Angola over the rest of the year and on how much we think it is appropriate to buy," he told a news conference.
"The other important thing... is the final nature of the agreement, if we can get that finalised in terms of the presidential decree and the government resolution."
